account:
Today has mostly followed the town's usual business. I visited the market, kept lunch at home, returned for accounts, and visited my neighbour for afternoon tea at the east-bank cottage beside the ferry landing. I have now returned to the office at 17:00, late for my 16:30 appointment.

There was some confusion about the tea address: the secretary had searched dockside cottages and asked warehouse workers without identifying my host. My neighbour personally confirmed the cottage at (16,-60,105), and I eventually conveyed that clearly to the secretary. I see no evidence that this confusion was anything more than missed communication.

The accounts review remains unfinished. The secretary had no figures supplied and asked where the ledger was. I checked the treasury and found 128 emeralds but no ledger. I do not know where the accounts records are; their absence from that chest is not evidence of wrongdoing.

The innkeeper requested a community gathering tomorrow at 18:00 in the great hall. I approved it, and the secretary said it was recorded in the appointment book. The innkeeper also wanted to discuss catering privately with the secretary, apparently to arrange that gathering. I have no knowledge of their private discussion.

The only unusual local report came from my neighbour at tea: they had heard a vague mention near the bakery of a bridge or port change, without a clear source. They explicitly did not regard it as confirmed news. No such public change has been announced to me, and I do not know who might be involved or what the supposed change is for. I intend to ask the secretary for reliable information rather than spread the rumour as fact. Otherwise my neighbour described a peaceful day of walks and greetings around the bakery, plaza, and dock.
